title: Session 2 - Participant 14 User + Claude Behavior Graph
goal: Get custom lists of R1 or R2 universities whose grants offices maintain a list of freelance editors for faculty to use, along with details on how to apply to be added to each one.

session_goal_achievement.Why or why not: Claude eventually returned this information, but not with as many universities as I had asked for or hoped.It returned many potential R1 and R2 universities that maintain lists of freelance editors for grant editing, along with details of how to apply.

Step 1.step_name: Search for 25 universities whose grants offices maintain a list of freelance editors for faculty to use
Step 1.step_action: Return a list of 25 universities whose grants offices maintain a list of freelance editors for faculty to use

nodes.label: Define the freelance-editor-list research goal and scope
nodes.detail: After logging back into Claude, the user states the overall goal (custom lists of R1/R2 universities whose grants offices maintain freelance-editor rosters for faculty, plus how to apply) and the specific Step 1 ask: search for 25 such universities and return them as a PDF.

nodes.label: Research candidate universities and compile the PDF deliverable
nodes.detail: Searches the web for university grants offices, writing centers, and faculty-development units that maintain freelance or independent editor rosters, verifies candidate institutions, then compiles the findings into a sectioned PDF covering verified research-office and writing-center lists, dead-end entries, and a completeness note. Delivers the PDF while noting that only 16 institutions were verified rather than the requested 25.

nodes.label: Review the delivered list against the requested scope
nodes.detail: The user opens the 9-page PDF in a full-screen viewer and reads through its sections and entries (e.g. the University of Michigan College of Engineering listing), evaluating that it falls short of the requested 25 universities and noticing a questionable R1/R2 inclusion before replying.

Step 2.step_name: Update list if any universities are not R1 or R2
Step 2.step_action: Replace any universities on the list that are not R1 or R2

nodes.label: Request removal of in-house-only entries and R1/R2 verification
nodes.detail: The user asks Claude to drop universities that only offer in-house editing and to double-check that every remaining school is genuinely R1 or R2, returning just the corrected university list in PDF form.

nodes.label: Re-verify Carnegie R1/R2 classifications and rebuild the list
nodes.detail: Claude runs targeted web_search calls to re-check classifications, confirming Lehigh is newly R1 (2025 cycle) and that Wesleyan fails the R2 threshold, then rebuilds the document (build_list.py) into a 14-university, all-R1 PDF.

nodes.label: Review the generated university editor-list PDF
Review the corrected 14-university R1 list
nodes.detail: The user opens Universities_With_Freelance_Editor_Lists.pdf and reads through the corrected, confirmed-R1 roster before raising a new question about the nature of the entries.

nodes.label: Question whether every roster is specifically grant-editing focused
nodes.detail: The user asks Claude whether all 14 listed rosters are actually for grant editing specifically, noting that some entries seem more general-purpose.

nodes.label: Explain the grant-focus spectrum and propose regrouping the list
nodes.detail: Claude explains that the roster spans genuinely grant-focused services, general research-office lists, and general academic editing where grant work is incidental, and offers to regroup the PDF into tiers reflecting this.

nodes.label: Review Claude's assessment of the grant-focus spectrum
Approve the proposed grant-focus regrouping
nodes.detail: The user confirms with a brief 'yes,' approving Claude's plan to reorganize the list by grant focus.

nodes.label: Rebuild the list as a three-tier, color-coded grouping by grant focus
nodes.detail: Claude reruns the build (build_list2.py) to reorganize the same 14 universities into green/amber/general tiers, flagging which entries are genuinely grant-focused (e.g. Iowa State, Wayne State) versus general academic editing (e.g. UNC, Duke).

nodes.label: Review the reorganized, tiered university list
nodes.detail: The user reviews the newly tiered PDF directly in a separate viewer tab, reading through the research-office-list and general-academic-editing sections before moving to the next request.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning:
Source a1: Requests list of 25 R1/R2 universities whose grants offices keep freelance editor lists
Target b9: Outputs the final list of universities. 
Reasoning: User refines the list. Accepts the final PDF with no modifications.

Step 3.step_name: Tell me how to apply to be added to the freelance editor list for each listed university
Step 3.step_action: Provide instructions for each university on how to be added to freelance editor list

nodes.label: Request a how-to-apply table for every listed university
nodes.detail: Having briefly re-checked the Step 3 requirement in the workflow planning document, the user asks Claude to provide, as a PDF table, instructions for how to apply to each university's freelance editor list.

nodes.label: Research verified application contact points and build the how-to-apply table
nodes.detail: Claude runs further web_search calls to pin down actual application routes, then builds build_apply.py, producing How_To_Apply_Freelance_Editor_Lists.pdf with a 'Route' column (open form / named contact / direct inquiry) for each university.

nodes.label: Review the how-to-apply table for completeness and documentation level
nodes.detail: The user reads through the delivered table, noting that only UNC has a true self-service application while most others require a named contact or a cold inquiry, before deciding what to revise.

Step 4.step_action: Follow instructions for how to revise the table to make it more clear

nodes.label: Request UCSB's removal and direct email contacts in place of general summaries
nodes.detail: The user asks Claude to delete UC Santa Barbara (no personal connection there) and to replace the general apply-by-summary text with direct email contacts so they do not have to look up details themselves.

nodes.label: Verify real email addresses via web search without fabricating any
nodes.detail: Claude explicitly declines to guess at email addresses, runs additional web_search calls to find genuinely published contacts, and rebuilds the table (build_contacts.py) into a 13-university version with verified (green) and office-only (amber) contact entries.

nodes.label: Review the university freelance-editor application guide
Review the revised contacts table with verified emails
nodes.detail: The user reviews Freelance_Editor_List_Application_Contacts.pdf, checking which of the 13 remaining universities now have a verified direct email versus only a named office.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning:
Source c1: Requests instructions on how to apply to each university's list
Target d2: Outputs Freelance_editor_list_application_contacts.pdf 
Reasoning: c2 gives general methods. d1 asks for direct emails, and drops some universities. User accepts d2 without modifcations

Step 5.step_name: Based upon my instructions, provide a second table with the top 10 of these universities
Step 5.step_action: Update the list to the top 10 universities to focus on

nodes.label: Request narrowing the list to the top 10 universities
nodes.detail: The user asks Claude to update the list down to just the top 10 universities to focus on.

nodes.label: Rank and select the top 10 by grant focus, reachability, and value
nodes.detail: Claude builds build_top10.py and ranks the 13 remaining universities by expected return, producing a ranked top-10 (UC Davis, Michigan, WashU, Wayne State, Iowa State, Emory, Johns Hopkins, Lehigh, UNC, Missouri) and dropping UCSB, Colorado Denver, Rochester, and Duke.

nodes.label: Review the ranked top-10 target list
nodes.detail: The user reviews Top10_Freelance_Editor_Lists_To_Target.pdf and its stated ranking rationale before deciding on the next request.

nodes.label: Request cutting UNC and drafting a customized application from a personal website
nodes.detail: The user asks to cut UNC from the list (it wants local editors and the user lives far away), and asks Claude to draft a customizable application, pointing it to their personal website for background material.

nodes.label: Gather the user's background and draft customized application emails
nodes.detail: Fetches the user's personal website to ground the outreach in their actual professional background and credentials, then drafts three customized application email templates tailored to different university office types: a default research-office version, a process-question version for Wayne State, and a publishing-focused version for Emory.

nodes.label: Review the customized application email drafts
Flag confusing details and request stronger emphasis on qualifications
Revise the drafts and update the top-10 list to drop UNC and add Rochester
nodes.detail: Claude clarifies the third-person/contact-form confusion, edits the drafts via str_replace to foreground the funded-proposal record, and -- as a side effect of cutting UNC -- also updates the Step 5 Top10 PDF, promoting University of Rochester into the #9 slot and re-presenting it.

nodes.label: Review the revised drafts and updated top-10 list
nodes.detail: The user reviews the updated email drafts and the revised Top10 PDF (UNC out, Rochester in) before deciding how the deliverables should be packaged.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning:
Source e1: Requests the top 10 university list. 
Target f5: Outputs an updated Top10.pdf, with refinements requested by user. 
Reasoning: e2 delivers the ranked top 10, f1 refines list, user accepts f5's final version

nodes.label: Request PDF output instead of inline chat drafts
nodes.detail: The user asks Claude to output the drafts as PDF files going forward rather than as text in the chat window.

nodes.label: Compile the complete application pack PDF
nodes.detail: Claude builds build_pack.py and delivers a multi-section Application_Pack_Freelance_Editor_Lists.pdf (email drafts per university, a separate Iowa State vendor-registration note, and listing profiles with [NUMBER]/[AGENCIES] placeholders), alongside the updated Top10 PDF.

nodes.label: Review the completed application pack
nodes.detail: The user reads through the full application pack PDF, including its email-vs-listing-profile distinction and the per-university draft assignments, before giving wording feedback.

nodes.label: Flag that describing experience as 'real' reads as defensive
nodes.detail: The user comments that it looks odd to write about their 'real' experience, flagging the word choice as a tone problem in the application pack.

nodes.label: Remove defensive qualifiers throughout the application pack
nodes.detail: Claude agrees that 'real' is defensive since it plants the doubt it is trying to answer, and removes every instance of 'real,' 'genuinely,' and 'nominal' via a series of str_replace edits, re-presenting the updated Application_Pack_Freelance_Editor_Lists.pdf.

nodes.label: Review the updated application pack

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning:
Source: f1 Requests a customized application draft based on the user's website
Target g2: Outputs the final application pack pdf
Reasoning: User accepts g2 after multiple refinements without modifying pdf.

nodes.label: Confirm the revised wording reads better
Affirm the wording revision and confirm the application pack is ready
Review Claude's final assessment of the application pack
Ask for an estimate of typical reply times
nodes.detail: The user asks how much time, on average, each university contact is likely to take to reply.

nodes.label: Reason through expected reply timing without fabricating data
nodes.detail: Claude explicitly notes it has no real data on reply times and instead reasons qualitatively about academic-calendar timing and recipient type, avoiding invented statistics.

nodes.label: Review Claude's assessment of reply timing and follow-up strategy
Ask whether to delay applying until August
nodes.detail: The user asks whether they should wait until August to send the applications, based on Claude's prior reasoning about timing.

nodes.label: Advise sending applications soon rather than delaying
nodes.detail: Claude reverses its earlier framing, arguing that email does not expire in an inbox and that momentum matters more than guessed timing, recommending the user send soon rather than wait.

nodes.label: Close the session with thanks
nodes.detail: The user thanks Claude twice in closing, and Claude reflects that the user's own pushback (on the 'real' wording and on the August-delay advice) measurably improved the final output; the recording ends shortly after.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning:
Source g7: Asks how long contacts typically take to reply
Target g11: Advises application timeline 
Reasoning: g8 gives no definite answer. User asks follow up question and accepts with "Ok"
